chunks: What al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad narrated from Aḥmad ibn Abī Bashīr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: When the sun passes the meridian in the length of the day, may a man perform the ẓuhr and ʿaṣr prayers? He said: Yes, and I like that he do that every day.

key_terms.أُحِبُّ: I prefer or like; indicating the Imam’s stated preference
key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose decline marks the beginning of the prayer time
key_terms.زَالَتِ: declined from the meridian; referring to the sun passing midday
key_terms.طُولِ النَّهَارِ: the span or length of the day

ai.seo_question: When the sun declines from the meridian, is it permissible to perform both ẓuhr and ʿaṣr prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith states that once the sun has declined from the meridian, a person may perform both the ẓuhr and ʿaṣr prayers. It also indicates the Imam’s preference for doing so regularly each day, reflecting a ruling related to the timing of salat (prayer).
